newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on Nasdaq losses.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on Nasdaq losses.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed mostly lower on Tuesday in the wake of declines in Israeli shares traded on Nasdaq, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 0.65 percent, or 1.20 points, to 184.05 on turnover of 56 million shekels against 48 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index fell 0.52 percent to 194.30.
"The market closed lower folowing the fall of Israeli shares traded on Nasdaq. Teva's decline pushed the market downwards," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank
Teva, the second-most active share, fell 4.0 percent to 128,470 on turnover of 6.0 million shekels after its issue traded on Nasdaq dropped 5.4 percent on Monday.

"Trading was very mixed today and there is much uncertainty in the market. We are waiting to see if the government will approve the budget despite the heavy opposition of coalition partners," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
The Treasury presented to parliament the 1997 budget that includes 4.9 billion shekels in spending cuts.
"Investors are also waiting to see what will happen with the talks with the Palestinians. Overall the makret is very nervous and activity is minimal," Nahum said.
Israel and the PLO have failed in three weeks of talks to seal a deal on terms for an Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
The most active share was Blue Square Chain Stores, which gained 0.5 percent to 2,514 on volume of 6.6 million shekels. Traders said foreign investors where the main buyers.
Koor Industries lost 1.25 percent to 28,111 on turnover of 2.3 million shekels.
